outlook: Grains slipped to new multi-week lows overnight after closing lower Tuesday, with harvest pressure under mostly dry Midwest weather still the main weight. As of 6 am CT, December corn was down about 2¼ cents near $4.60, November soybeans down about 3¼ cents near $12.45, and December Chicago wheat down 4 cents near $6.39. Soybeans have lagged even with steady Chinese buying, including a reported 612,000-tonne purchase announced Tuesday, while wheat is following corn and beans lower on ample world supply. ICE November canola eased about C$4 to C$776.70 overnight after Tuesday's drop to a near two-month low; Minneapolis December spring wheat settled Tuesday at $6.6175, down 8¼ cents.
